cards.raw0: <u>Vancomycin-resistant bacteria</u> typically spread resistance to other bacteria via {{c1::transposition::mechanism}}
cards.back: Typically, the resistance gene (e.g., VanA) and some flanking chromosomal DNA is incorporated into a plasmid (e.g., Tn1546) and transferred into a new bacterium (e.g., VRE → Staph aureus )

cards.front: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum often present with freckled and dry skin, extreme [ sunlight ] sensitivity, and [ corneal ] ulcers
cards.raw0: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum often present with freckled and dry skin, extreme {{c1::sunlight}} sensitivity, and {{c1::corneal}} ulcers
cards.back: Patients will typically be light skinned Corneal scarring/ulceration, hyperkeratotic lesions, freckles: [img] Photo credit: James Halpern, Bryan Hopping and Joshua M Brostoff , CC BY-SA 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum are at risk for which type(s) of skin cancer? [All :)]
cards.raw0:
Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum are at risk for which type(s) of skin cancer?

{{c1::All :)}}
cards.back: Melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, and squamous carcinoma [img]

cards.front: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum cannot repair [pyrimidine dimers] formed as a result of UV-B exposure
cards.raw0: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum cannot repair {{c1::pyrimidine dimers}} formed as a result of UV-B exposure
cards.back: - This card used to say thymidine, but AMBOSS + FA23 confirm pyrimidine dimers are formed (Dec 2023) - These patients either have a defective enzyme that recognizes helix distortions (XPC / XPA) or have a defective excision endonuclease (XPB, XPD-XPG) [img] Photo credit: derivative work: Mouagip (talk)DNA_UV_mutation.gif: NASA/David Herring This W3C-unspecified vector image was created with Adobe Illustrator. , Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons [img] Photo credit: Jones, Daniel & Baxter, Bonnie. (2016). Bipyrimidine Signatures as a Photoprotective Genome Strategy in G + C-rich Halophilic Archaea. Life. 6. 37. 10.3390/life6030037 . CC BY 4.0

cards.front: Homologous recombination occurs [ after ] S phase of the cell cycle, using a(n) [ sister chromatid ] as a template
cards.raw0: Homologous recombination occurs {{c1::after::before / after?}} S phase of the cell cycle, using a(n) {{c2::sister chromatid}} as a template
cards.back: Because it needs sister chromatids, this must occur after S phase

cards.front: In homologous recombination , dsDNA breaks are recognized by the [ ATM ] protein and the [ FA core ] complex , which activate [ BRCA1/2 ] to recruit enzymes to repair the break
cards.raw0: In homologous recombination, dsDNA breaks are recognized by the {{c2::ATM}} protein and the {{c2::FA core}} complex, which activate {{c1::BRCA1/2}} to recruit enzymes to repair the break
cards.back: Thus patients with BRCA1/2, FANC, ATM mutations are susceptible to damage by ionizing radiation [img] Photo credit: Chaya5260 , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons [img] Photo credit: Hannes Lans, Jurgen A Marteijn and Wim Vermeulen , CC BY 2.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Homologous recombination is defective in breast/ovarian cancers with [BRCA1/2] mutations
cards.raw0: Homologous recombination is defective in breast/ovarian cancers with {{c1::BRCA1/2}} mutations
cards.back: Also in Fanconi anemia [img] Photo credit: Chaya5260 , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Is homologous recombination error prone ? [No]
cards.raw0:
Is homologous recombination error prone?

{{c1::No}}
cards.back: - However, this may result in a unique manifestation of loss of heterozygosity - This can occur when the mutation is in the intact strand being used as a template, and the damaged DNA (which was encoding for a normal protein) is fixed using the mutation

cards.front: Nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) occurs [throughout the cell cycle]
cards.raw0: Nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) occurs {{c1::throughout the cell cycle::when in the cell cycle}}
cards.back: - This card used to say before S phase of cell cycle, but AMBOSS confirms this occurs throughout the cell cycle (Sept 2023) - There is NO requirement for homology

cards.front: In nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ), dsDNA breaks are recognized by [ ATM ], recruiting the MRN complex which then recruits the [Artemis] protein and various others to help repair the damage
cards.raw0: In nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ), dsDNA breaks are recognized by {{c2::ATM}}, recruiting the MRN complex which then recruits the {{c1::Artemis}} protein and various others to help repair the damage
cards.back: - NHEJ is crucial for VDJ recombination to work, thus patients with defective NHEJ can manifest with SCID - Artemis, XLF, Pol h and u, cut ends so MRN complex can bind - Cut ends are ligated by DNA ligase IV [img] Photo credit: Hannes Lans, Jurgen A Marteijn and Wim Vermeulen , CC BY 2.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Is nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) error prone ? [Yes]
cards.raw0:
Is nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) error prone?

{{c1::Yes}}
cards.back: HIGHLY error prone; this has no template strand to compare to

cards.front: Nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) is defective in [ ataxia telangiectasia ] and might be defective in [ severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)]
cards.raw0: Nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) is defective in {{c2::ataxia telangiectasia}} and might be defective in {{c1::severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)}}
cards.back: e.g., defect in the Artemis protein or ATM [img] Photo credit: Hannes Lans, Jurgen A Marteijn and Wim Vermeulen , CC BY 2.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: BRCA1 and BRCA2 are tumor suppressors that are involved in mediating the [homologous recombination (HR)] pathway of DNA repair
cards.raw0: BRCA1 and BRCA2 are tumor suppressors that are involved in mediating the {{c1::homologous recombination (HR)}} pathway of DNA repair
cards.back: - This is a form of double stranded break repair that requires a template strand (thus must occur after S phase) - dsDNA breaks can be detected by ATM and the FA Core Complex, acting as a nidus to recruit BRCA enzymes, which then recruit RAD51 and others to fix the break [img] Photo credit: Chaya5260 , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: The [BLM helicase] is involved in regulating homologous recombination , and when mutated causes Bloom syndrome
cards.raw0: The {{c1::BLM helicase::enzyme}} is involved in regulating homologous recombination, and when mutated causes Bloom syndrome

cards.front: Patients with Bloom syndrome present with cafe-au-lait spots, rash from [sun] exposure, and [short] stature
cards.raw0: Patients with Bloom syndrome present with cafe-au-lait spots, rash from {{c1::sun}} exposure, and {{c2::short}} stature
cards.back: [img] I mage(s) licensed by DermNet and used with permission, CC-BY-NC-ND 3.0 NZ

cards.front: Because patients with Bloom syndrome have a dysfunctional BLM helicase enzyme , they are at great risk of developing [cancer]
cards.raw0: Because patients with Bloom syndrome have a dysfunctional BLM helicase enzyme, they are at great risk of developing {{c1::cancer}}
cards.back: Mutations accumulate quickly due to an enormous increase in exchange events between homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids; patients have high amounts of leukemias, lymphomas, and/or carcinomas

cards.raw0: Patients with Bloom syndrome are associated with premature {{c1::aging}}
cards.back: These patients have shortened telomeres

cards.front: Patients with ataxia-telangiectasia have vitiligo, granulomas, and a high recurrence of [sinopulmonary] infections
cards.raw0: Patients with ataxia-telangiectasia have vitiligo, granulomas, and a high recurrence of {{c1::sinopulmonary::location}} infections
cards.back: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections can lead to bronchiectasis; due to being IgA, IgG, and IgE deficient [img]

cards.front: Slippage in a template strand will cause a(n) [deletion]
cards.raw0: Slippage in a template strand will cause a(n) {{c1::deletion}}
cards.back: Whereas slippage in a replicated strand will cause an insertion

cards.front: Slippage in a replicated strand will cause a(n) [insertion]
cards.raw0: Slippage in a replicated strand will cause a(n) {{c1::insertion}}
cards.back: Whereas slippage in a template strand will cause a deletion

cards.front: Depurination results in the loss of [purine] bases
cards.raw0: Depurination results in the loss of {{c1::purine}} bases
cards.back: - Occurs thousands of times per day - Sugar phosphate stays in the backbone
